headings.title: Classification as misdemeanor or class E felony

headings.title: Elements of second-degree child sexual abuse promotion
headings.reviewNote: Defines promoting child sexual abuse material in the second degree involving material portraying a minor.

headings.title: Classification as class D or class B felony and probation bar
headings.reviewNote: Classifies offense as class D felony, or class B felony if knowingly promoted to a minor, and bars probation eligibility.

headings.title: Elements of possession of child sexual abuse material
headings.reviewNote: Defines possession of child sexual abuse material as knowingly or recklessly possessing child sexual abuse material or obscene material portraying a minor under eighteen.

headings.title: Classification as class D or class B felony
headings.reviewNote: Classifies possession of one still image as class D felony, and possession of over twenty still images, any moving image, or repeat offense as class B felony.

headings.title: Separate punishments for each item possessed
headings.reviewNote: Subjects a person who commits possession of child sexual abuse material to separate punishments for each item possessed.

entries.reviewSummary: Rewrote subsections 2-3 to match archived text (class D for 1 still image / class B for >20 still images, moving image, or repeat; separate punishments per item) and noted 2023 State v. Ingram annotation.

headings.title: State or court custody of child pornography or abuse material
headings.reviewNote: Requires child pornography (prior to August 28, 2026) or child sexual abuse material in criminal proceedings to remain in state or court care, custody, and control.

headings.title: Denial of defense reproduction and reasonable inspection access
headings.reviewNote: Directs courts to deny defense copying or reproduction requests notwithstanding Rule 25.03 if the state makes material reasonably available for inspection at a government facility.

entries.reviewSummary: Rewrote both subsections from scratch to match archived text on state/court custody of child pornography/CSAM and denial of defense copying with reasonable facility inspection access.

headings.title: Elements of furnishing pornographic materials to minors
headings.reviewNote: Defines furnishing pornographic material to minors by furnishing material or performances knowing or recklessly disregarding minority, or via computer to a known minor.

headings.title: Peace officer masquerading as minor not a defense
headings.reviewNote: Provides that it is not a defense that the person furnished pornographic material is a peace officer masquerading as a minor.

headings.title: Classification as class A misdemeanor or class E felony
headings.reviewNote: Classifies furnishing or attempting to furnish pornographic material to minors as a class A misdemeanor, or class E felony for prior chapter 573, 566, or 568 offense.

entries.reviewSummary: Rewrote shifted/fabricated subsections 2-3 to match archived text (peace officer masquerading as minor not a defense; class A misdemeanor or class E felony for repeat ch. 573/566/568 offense).

headings.title: Admissible evidence on appeal, value, acceptance, and purpose
headings.reviewNote: Makes evidence admissible on predominant appeal, literary/artistic/political/scientific value, public acceptance, prurient advertising, and creator or promoter purpose.

headings.title: Admissibility of creator, promoter, or expert testimony
headings.reviewNote: Makes testimony of author, creator, promoter, furnisher, publisher, or experts admissible on obscenity or child sexual abuse material issues.

headings.title: Methods for determining age under seventeen or eighteen
headings.reviewNote: Permits court or jury to determine whether a person was under seventeen or eighteen by personal or image inspection, witness or expert testimony, or other lawful method.

headings.title: No obscenity-test showing required in child promotion cases
headings.reviewNote: Provides that prosecutions for promoting child pornography or child sexual abuse material require no showing of prurient interest, lack of serious value, or patent offensiveness.

entries.reviewSummary: Rewrote all 4 mismatched subsections to match archived text (admissible evidence factors, creator/expert testimony, age determination methods, and no obscenity-test showing for child promotion).

headings.title: Elements of public display of explicit sexual material
headings.reviewNote: Defines public display of explicit sexual material by recklessly displaying material readily visible from public ways, others' property, or general retail areas, or failing to promptly remove it.

headings.title: Classification as class A misdemeanor or class E felony
headings.reviewNote: Classifies public display of explicit sexual material as a class A misdemeanor, or class E felony for a prior offense under this section.

headings.title: Each day of violation as separate offense
headings.reviewNote: Provides that each day there is a violation of this section constitutes a separate offense.

entries.reviewSummary: Rewrote all 3 fabricated subsections to match archived text on public display of explicit sexual material, class A misdemeanor/class E felony penalties, and daily separate offenses.

headings.title: Elements of coercing acceptance of obscene material

headings.title: Classification as class E felony

entries.reviewSummary: Verified verbatim against archived text (effective 1-01-17).

headings.title: Civil action for declaratory judgment and injunction
headings.reviewNote: Permits prosecuting, circuit, or city attorneys to bring a civil circuit court action for declaratory judgment and injunction against chapter violations.

headings.title: Venue in circuit court of residence or violation
headings.reviewNote: Restricts venue to the circuit court of the county where a defendant resides or where the violation is occurring or about to occur.

headings.title: Intervention as of right by promoter, furnisher, or displayer
headings.reviewNote: Permits any promoter, furnisher, or displayer (or prospective one) of the material or performance to intervene as of right as a party defendant.

headings.title: Expedited trial, two-day decision, and prior adversary hearing
headings.reviewNote: Mandates expedited trial and appellate consideration, trial within one week of joinder, decision within two days, and prior adversary hearing before any injunction.

headings.title: Limitation on use of final declaration to injunction basis
headings.reviewNote: Limits use of a final declaration under this section solely to forming the basis for an injunction.

headings.title: Inapplicability of conflicting rules and bench trial requirement
headings.reviewNote: Precludes inconsistent procedural rules and specifies there is no right to a jury trial in section proceedings.

entries.reviewSummary: Rewrote subsections 1-5 to match archived text (permissive civil action, venue, intervention as of right, expedited 1-week trial/2-day decision/prior adversary hearing, and injunction-only use of declaration).

headings.title: Separate display area requirement for specified video reproductions
headings.reviewNote: Requires video reproduction devices catering to morbid violence or pornographic for minors to be displayed in a separate area.

headings.title: Prohibition on sales or rentals to minors under seventeen
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits the sale or rental of morbidly violent or pornographic video reproduction devices to persons under seventeen years of age.

headings.title: Penalties classification for display and sales violations
headings.reviewNote: Designates violations as infractions, unless conduct constitutes promoting obscenity or furnishing pornographic materials to minors.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified against archived text and 1992 Video Software Dealers Assn. v. Webster annotation without enforceability claims.

headings.title: Definitions of indecent and obscene

headings.title: Elements of obscene or indecent commercial messaging
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits making obscene or indecent comments or suggestions by telephone for commercial purposes or permitting telephone facilities to be so used.

headings.title: Classification as misdemeanor or class E felony
headings.reviewNote: Classifies offense as a class A misdemeanor, elevated to a class E felony for repeat violations, treating each violation separately.

headings.title: Exemption for telecommunications companies
headings.reviewNote: Exempts telecommunications companies over whose facilities prohibited communications are transmitted from section prohibitions and penalties.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified verbatim against archived text (effective 1-01-17).

headings.title: Citation as Evan's Voice Act

headings.title: Elements of nonconsensual dissemination of private sexual images
headings.reviewNote: Defines the offense of intentionally disseminating private sexual images of an identifiable person without consent to harass, threaten, or coerce.

headings.title: Exemptions for criminal investigation, reporting, or public setting
headings.reviewNote: Exempts dissemination for lawful criminal investigations, reporting unlawful conduct, voluntary public exposure, or lawful public purposes.

headings.title: Liability limitation for computer, mobile, and broadband providers
headings.reviewNote: Excludes liability for interactive computer services (47 U.S.C. 230(f)(2)), public or private mobile services, and telecommunications network or broadband providers solely for user content.

headings.title: Forfeiture under sections 513.600 to 513.660
headings.reviewNote: Subjects persons convicted under this section to forfeiture under sections 513.600 to 513.660.

headings.title: Classification as class D felony or class C felony
headings.reviewNote: Classifies nonconsensual dissemination of private sexual images as a class D felony, or class C felony if the image is of a minor or vulnerable person.

headings.title: Private cause of action for statutory or actual damages
headings.reviewNote: Creates a private cause of action for depicted persons awarding $10,000 or actual damages (whichever is greater) plus attorney's fees, with humiliation or embarrassment sufficient.

headings.title: Elements of threatening nonconsensual dissemination of sexual images
headings.reviewNote: Defines threatening the nonconsensual dissemination of private sexual images to gain anything of value or coerce action or inaction.

headings.title: Tiered felony classifications and class B felony enhancements
headings.reviewNote: Classifies offense as class E felony (first), class D (second), class C (third+), or class B felony if depicting a minor or vulnerable person or proximately causing serious physical injury or death.

headings.title: Prohibition on suspended sentence for repeat offenders

headings.title: Elements of promoting child in sexual performance
headings.reviewNote: Defines promoting a sexual performance by a child under eighteen by promoting, producing, or directing a performance including sexual conduct.

headings.title: Classification as class C felony
headings.reviewNote: Classifies promoting a sexual performance by a child as a class C felony.

headings.title: Prohibition on suspended sentence for repeat offenders
headings.reviewNote: Bars courts from granting suspended imposition or execution of sentence to a person previously found guilty under this section.

entries.reviewSummary: Rewrote subsections 1-3 to match archived text (child under 18, class C felony, and SIS/SES bar for repeat offenders; formerly 568.090).

headings.reviewNote: Defines patronizing a sexual performance by a child as obtaining, soliciting, or participating in a sexual performance by a child under eighteen.

headings.reviewNote: Classifies patronizing a sexual performance by a child as a class C felony.

headings.title: Elements of failure to report child sexual abuse material

headings.reviewNote: Classifies failure to report child sexual abuse material as a class B misdemeanor.

headings.title: Local sales tax on adult cabarets and voter approval
headings.reviewNote: Permits counties and St. Louis City to impose a voter-approved sales tax up to ten percent of gross receipts on adult cabarets to defray background check costs.

headings.title: Ballot language and effective date upon majority vote
headings.reviewNote: Prescribes ballot submission table and makes voter-approved tax effective on the first day of the second calendar quarter after notice to director of revenue.

headings.title: Special trust fund deposit and permitted law enforcement uses
headings.reviewNote: Requires depositing tax revenue in a special trust fund for adult cabaret employee background checks and general sheriff law enforcement use, permitting lawful investment.

headings.title: Four-year termination of tax unless sooner abolished
headings.reviewNote: Terminates the tax four years after initial imposition unless sooner abolished by the city or county governing body.

headings.title: City and county background check tax trust fund distribution
headings.reviewNote: Creates the City and County Background Check Tax Trust Fund (less 1% state collection fee) and requires monthly distribution by the tenth day.

headings.title: Refunds, dishonored checks, and repeal notice retention
headings.reviewNote: Permits refunds and dishonored check redemption, requires ninety-day repeal notice, and allows two percent one-year retention upon abolition.

headings.title: Applicability of sections 32.085 and 32.087
headings.reviewNote: Applies sections 32.085 and 32.087 to the sales tax except as modified in this section.

headings.title: Definition of city
headings.reviewNote: Defines city as any city not within a county.

entries.reviewSummary: Rewrote all 8 fabricated subsections to match archived text on voter-approved adult cabaret sales tax (up to 10%), ballot table, trust fund, 4-year sunset, refunds/abolition, and 2001 Miss Kitty's Saloon annotation.

headings.title: Local authority to set adult cabaret minimum admission age
headings.reviewNote: Permits any city not within a county or any county to establish a minimum age limit for admission into adult cabarets.

headings.title: Local authority to require adult cabaret security personnel
headings.reviewNote: Permits any city not within a county or any county to require security personnel on adult cabaret premises.

headings.title: Local authority to require random employee drug testing
headings.reviewNote: Permits any city not within a county or any county to require adult cabaret employers to conduct random blood or urine testing for illegal substances.

headings.title: Local authority to prohibit live public nudity within ten feet
headings.reviewNote: Permits any city not within a county or any county to prohibit live public nudity within ten feet of any observer.

headings.title: Local authority to prohibit sexual displays or nudity in cabarets
headings.reviewNote: Permits any city not within a county or any county to prohibit public display of sexual intercourse, deviate sexual intercourse, or nudity in adult cabarets.

headings.title: Prohibition on persons under nineteen dancing in adult cabaret
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits persons under nineteen years of age from dancing in an adult cabaret and prohibits proprietors from permitting them to do so.

headings.title: Classification as class A misdemeanor
headings.reviewNote: Classifies violation of the section as a class A misdemeanor.

entries.reviewSummary: Rewrote both fabricated subsections to match archived text prohibiting persons under nineteen from dancing in adult cabarets (class A misdemeanor).

headings.title: Statutory purpose of sexually oriented business regulations
headings.reviewNote: States purpose of sections 573.525 to 573.537 to prevent adverse secondary effects of sexually oriented businesses without restricting First Amendment access or condoning obscenity.

headings.title: Legislative findings on adverse secondary effects
headings.reviewNote: Sets out legislative findings regarding adverse secondary effects of sexually oriented businesses and the state's substantial interest in preventing or abating them.

entries.reviewSummary: Rewrote both fabricated subsections to match archived text on statutory purpose and legislative findings for sexually oriented business regulations.

headings.title: Distance restrictions from schools, churches, daycares, and residences
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits establishing a sexually oriented business within one thousand feet of schools, churches, daycares, parks, or residences.

headings.title: Criminal disqualification from establishing sexually oriented business
headings.reviewNote: Bars establishment of sexually oriented businesses by persons with influential interests who have specified felony or sex offense convictions.

headings.title: Prohibition on nudity in sexually oriented businesses
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits any person from knowingly appearing in a state of nudity inside a sexually oriented business.

headings.title: Stage height and separation requirements for seminude employees
headings.reviewNote: Requires semi-nude employees to remain on a fixed stage at least eighteen inches high and six feet from patrons in a room of at least six hundred square feet.

headings.title: Prohibition on physical contact between employees and patrons
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits semi-nude employees from knowingly or intentionally touching a patron or a patron's clothing in a sexually oriented business.

headings.title: Visibility and configuration standards for viewing rooms
headings.reviewNote: Requires unobstructed direct line of sight from operator stations (max 32 sq ft), staffed monitoring, and removal of obstructions in video-exhibiting viewing rooms.

headings.title: Compliance grace period for preexisting nonconforming premises
headings.reviewNote: Grants nonconforming businesses one hundred eighty days after August 28, 2010 to comply with stage and building requirements while maintaining six-foot semi-nude separation.

headings.title: Prohibited operating hours between midnight and six a.m.
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits sexually oriented businesses from operating between the hours of 12:00 midnight and 6:00 a.m.

headings.title: Prohibition on alcohol sale or consumption on premises
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits selling, using, or consuming alcoholic beverages on the premises of a sexually oriented business.

headings.title: Prohibition on presence of minors under eighteen
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits allowing individuals under the age of eighteen on the premises of a sexually oriented business.

headings.title: Definitions of statutory terms
headings.reviewNote: Defines establish or establishment, influential interest, and viewing room for purposes of this section.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified all 11 subsections against archived text; corrected subsection 6 to 'viewing rooms', subsection 7 note to 180-day compliance period after August 28, 2010, and subsection 11 note to exact defined terms.

headings.title: Misdemeanor penalty, fine, imprisonment, and separate daily offenses
headings.reviewNote: Classifies violation of sections 573.525 to 573.537 as a misdemeanor punishable by up to $500 fine, 90 days imprisonment, or both, with each day and occurrence a separate offense.

headings.title: Declaration of public nuisance and injunctive remedies
headings.reviewNote: Declares repeatedly noncompliant sexually oriented businesses to be public nuisances subject to abatement injunctions.

headings.title: Preservation of legal and equitable state remedies
headings.reviewNote: Preserves the state's right to employ all legal and equitable remedies to prevent or remedy regulatory violations.

entries.reviewSummary: Corrected subsection 1 heading and note from class A misdemeanor to statutory unclassified misdemeanor (up to $500 fine, 90 days jail, or both; daily/occurrence separate offenses).

headings.title: Preservation of local authority to regulate adult businesses
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that sections 573.525 to 573.537 do not preempt political subdivisions from regulating sexually oriented businesses.

headings.title: Requirement of consistency with minimum state standards
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes local ordinances and regulations that comply with or exceed the minimum requirements of state statute.
